2026-11-27.title: Friday after the Sunday of the Annunciation
readings: Do not be weary in doing what is right
2026-11-27.verse: Therefore what God has joined together, let no one separate.
theo: Some Thessalonians, expecting the Lord's return at any moment, had stopped working and were living as busybodies. Paul reminds them that he and his companions worked “night and day” so as not to burden anyone, and gives a blunt rule: anyone unwilling to work should not eat. Then a word for all who are tired of doing good: “Brothers and sisters, do not be weary in doing what is right.” Faith makes us responsible, not idle.

When the Pharisees ask about divorce, Jesus takes them back beyond Moses' concession, which was given “because of your hardness of heart”, to the beginning of creation: God made them male and female, and the two become one flesh. “Therefore what God has joined together, let no one separate.” Christian marriage is a covenant God himself seals; in the Syriac tradition the crowning of bride and groom shows that their union is holy and royal.
outline: “What God has joined together, let no one separate.”
live: Pray today for couples in difficulty, including in your own family.
Finish one task you have neglected.
2026-11-27.prayer: Lord Jesus, you blessed marriage from the beginning. Strengthen husbands and wives in faithful love, soften hard hearts, and keep us from growing weary in doing what is right. Amen.

2026-11-27.question: Where am I tired of doing good?

homily: Dear friends, some Thessalonians, expecting the Lord's return at any moment, had stopped working and were living as busybodies. Paul reminds them that he and his companions worked night and day so as not to burden anyone: anyone unwilling to work should not eat. Brothers and sisters, do not be weary in doing what is right (2 Thessalonians 3:8–13).

In the Gospel, when the Pharisees ask about divorce, Jesus goes back to the beginning: from the beginning of creation God made them male and female; the two shall become one flesh. Therefore what God has joined together, let no one separate (Mark 10:6–9).

Faithful work and faithful love: both are good preparation for the Lord's coming. Today do your work with joy; let husbands and wives say a word of thanks to each other; and let us pray for couples who are struggling in their marriage. Amen.
